To validate the Release status is populating after completion of the mentioned reviews: ECO Supervisor, Documentation ,Design Space, L3, L4 & Homologation Reviews(Certification, CO2, Emission, Third Party). 👥 Role TT/PDM-Author Documentation. TT/Approver Co2.Homologation.TT/Approver Emission.Homologation.TT/Approver Certification.Homologation.TT/Approver eDrive.Homologation.TT/Approver Feature. Design Space.TT/ Evaluator 👾Object​ Engineering change object (ECO) 🛠 Preconditions The Engineering Change Object (ECO) needs to be created in T.B Planner and transferred to PLATON. To Perform this test case the ECO Should have the mentioned attributes populated in T.B Planner Properties tab: 1)Design Space/Approval Party Should be CS 2)Lead E3 Should be True 3)Lead E4 Should be True The ECO Should have the Group Type as AB, AC, AE, AF, AG, AK, AS, DA, DP, GE, M1, M2, M3, M4, M5, ME, OP . Object types allowed to attach to ECO SA Revision, Part/Assembly Design Revision, Component Revision, Raw Part Design Revision, Flexible Part Desin Revision, Standard Part Design Revision. The solution Item should have Engineering status before attaching to the ECO. ECO Should have valid pre-release checks before initiating the workflow. All the solution Items attached needs to be Release Ready before initiating the ECO Release Workflow-TT. The value of Leading Design Approval in Solution Item & the value of the attribute ffKf in TB Planner Properties should be the same before initiating the ECO Release workflow-TT 👍​ Expected Results The Engineering Change Order (ECO) will have different release statuses on it at various stages of the Workflow order based on the Approval/Rejections from the Reviewer's (In Engineering, System Check, In Evaluation, In Approval, Released). The object Revision attached in the solution Item must have Release status. Release Status should get populated in the ECO as well as the Revision which is added in the Solution Item & Respective datasets.

ECO should be created from TB Planner with a valid ECO number in TB planner properties tab. SA revision in releases state should be kept ready. All revisions should be "Set in Engineering" before linking them to ECO. ECO revision with revisions (UPS) in solutions folder. 👍​ Expected Results Engineering changes sent to Safira will be validated and a decision is sent from Safira whether if these changes can be implemented in Production or not. All PDF, TIF, SVG dataset files will be stored in ZGDOK along with successful completion of Release. If the ZGDOK transfer gets failed, then the release workflow will also halt and will remain incomplete.

Search & Open SA/Design Usage rev_0002 which is revised in Step 03 Click on Copy on primary tool bar SA/Design usage rev gets copied to clipboard Pre-requisites For ZGDOK Transfer: a) Select Design revision and then click on Edit->Check-out->Edit on Primary Tool bar. b) Search for the "ZGS" attribute on overview tab and Fill a value for it (Ex: 0001). c) Click on Edit->Save Edits and then Edit->Check-in to update attributes. Pre-requisites For Safira transfer: 1) Find number attribute must not be empty for all child in a BoM Structure. a) All modifiable attributes on Design revision should be visible. b) ZGS attribute should accept the value. c) All changes/updates on Design revision should be saved successfully. For ZGDOK Transfer: a) Select Design revision and navigate to Attachments tab of Design revision and Click Add to under Files section. b) Under New section, Click on select a file of type "TIF, PDF, SVG" and then click on Open. c) Fill all mandatory fields and Select the file type "TIF, PDF, SVG" and relation as "Specification" for these dataset types. d) If a UGPART dataset is available with Design revision, then to attach the mentioned file types "TIF, PDF, SVG" to existing UGPART, Select relation as "Rendering" for these dataset types. e) Click on Add to attach above Datasets with a relation. a) Attachments tab with different sections will be visible and Add panel should be displayed. b) File selected will be visible on Add panel. c, d) File type, relation should be updated on Add Panel and Add command should be enabled. e) Dataset should be visible under Files section on Attachment tab. Prerequisite: Part Revisions should be having "Engineering" State before adding to ECO revision (Refer Test case-87041 for Set In Engineering). Case2: a) Select ECO revision and navigate to Workflow tab to check the state. b) Verify the Decision from Safira in the Workflow tab a) The workflow will be on Hold for few minutes until a decision is received from Safira. b) If Decision is "F" from Safira, then the "ZGDOK workflow will be triggered". c) Release status will be assigned to ECO along with solution Items and then t he Datasets related to solution Items will be transferred to Zgdok. Note is the Dataset which is generally attached to Part/Assembly, Standard Part, Flexible Part, etc. objects in Smaragd & it is migrated as a Note form in PLATON. Group & Role: Group: Any Role: PDM-Author Preconditions: A user should have access to Smaragd (Source) System as well as PLATON (Target) System User should have read access for Note dataset/form at Source as well as Target Object Types: Note dataset (Smaragd & PLATON) Expected Result: Note dataset must be migrated from Source to Target. Remark attribute value must be mapped as per the mapping definition if Note dataset is not migrated.
test_steps: Login to Smaragd as well as PLATON using valid credentials User login is successful for both the Systems Smaragd: Search and Open an existing Part Master/ Standard Part Master/ Flexible Part Master which has version/s with Release State= Engineering or Released or Frozen (Scope of Migration) Object having versions with mentioned released status is searched & opened successfully. PLATON: a. Use Global Search & Find the item which corresponds to the same object opened in Step 2 b. Open using Open button. The corresponding object is searched at Target system Opened Successfully Smaragd & PLATON: Case 1: Smaragd- Check if the Note is attached to the version as Primary or Secondary Dataset Yes- Note Form should be available in PLATON Attachments- NOTE FORMS for the corresponding revision No- Note Form should not be available in PLATON Note dataset as a form should be migrated from Smaragd to PLATON Smaragd & PLATON: Case 2: a. Check if Note dataset is available in Smaragd with NoteTitle attribute value as 'Remark' b. Note down the value of attribute NoteData from Smaragd c. Verify if the Remark attribute value of corresponding revision in PLATON is matching with NoteData value in Smaragd (Step 2) Note dataset as form is not migrated in PLATON but Remark attribute value is mapped as per mapping definition

Click the " Attachments " navigational tab The "Attachments" view is visible in the work area In the " Files " and " Flexible Parts " sections the same PDF and Flexible Part should be attached/visible as for the source Revision. WAVE Geometry Linker is a means of associatively (or not if desired) linking (copying) geometry from one part into another. test_steps: Open Postman and paste the Teamcenter server URL in the URL tab Teamcenter URL is pasted successfully Login with valid credentials in Authorization tab to establish a connection to Teamcenter. Authentication is completed successfully Select the "PATCH" request in the query list to update attributes of a part available in Teamcenter PATCH request is selected successfully Enter Teamcenter Environment Base URL, Port ID with required Query to the right of HTTP methods (PATCH) section. Ex : http://172.28.1.9:11301/pxml/item/workflow Note : Teamcenter IP address with Port number of Respective Environment should be used Teamcenter URL with Query is added Navigate to Body Section, Select Raw and then format as JSON Input Format is selected successfully Case1: Enter the input in body section. If the "work_flow_template" attribute is either empty or absent from the request body, the value of the "release_state" attribute will be used to set the status. Case5: Provide a Part number with Released or pending state on it in Teamcenter and then Click on Send to process the request Ex: { "p4d_part_number": "R0283783", "item_revision_id": "0001", "release_state": "Pending", "work_flow_template":"" "dataset_uids":"" } A status message with "409 Conflict" will be displayed in the Body section below. Raw Part Design Revision Production Facility Design Revision Container Design Revision 🛠 Preconditions ECO should be created from TB Planner with a valid ECO number in TB planner properties tab. testcase_description: Objective: Prepare sales data in PLATON & upload NX data in form of STEP files and provide it to customer/supplier for downloads. Group & Role: Group: TT Role: PDM-Author Object: - Part/Assembly Pre-conditions: User must be able to Access NX as well as PLATON Active Workspace. User must have required Group/Role combinations in PLATON . Valid Design object must be available in the system before executing this Test Case: Refer: Test Case 192929 : 05.20_Business Scenario (185034)- Create Parts from SPIN Interface , before this Test case. Expected Results: User must be able to create simplified geometry for Third Party Customer or for a supplier.
test_steps: Login to NX managed mode with valid credentials (Group: TT, Role: PDM-Author) User login to NX Managed mode is successful Switch to Integrated Active Workspace from NX User is now in integrated AWC. Search & Open any Part/Assembly revision by Providing the Part Number in Global Search. Part/Assembly revision is search and open in PLATON. Click on Open in NX icon to open the Design / Component directly in NX. Part/Assembly is open in NX. Modify part/assembly as per requirement, (e.g adding 3D geometry etc.) Part/Assembly design is updated as per requirement in NX. Select geometry and assign Reference set ( 'FINAL_PART' ) to the 3D geometry. FINAL_PART reference set is assigned to 3D geometry. GO to "File->Export->STEP..." Export STEP File dialog opens. a. Select AP214 from Export To section b. Select folder location to save Step-file. c. Select any other option as per your requirement from dialog (this is optional step) d. Click on OK Step file is exported as mention location. Launch Native NX and open the exported Step file Files got opened a. Modify this step file as per requirement. b. Save and download this as part file. Data got modified and saved in form of part file(.prt) Login to Platon with valid credentials (Group: TT, Role: PDM-Author) User is able to login Search & Open the same Part/Assembly design (used in step3). Part/Assembly design revision should search and open. Select top node of structure-> Add->Secondary Component Add Secondary Component dialog open From Secondary Component Type LOV select "Sales" Fill the required filed and then click on Add. Note:- User can also add existing sales type secondary data from Palette/Search Secondary Component (Sales) is created. Note:- We can see Column "Occurrence Type" will show Sales value in it. a. Select the added Secondary Component and go to Attachment tab. b. go to File->Add->Upload File->Select File & upload .prt file saved in step 10. c. Select UGMASTER under Type. Data/part file is stored in form of NX format to secondary component Select the added "Secondary Component" and Open (Open the selection in NX) this to integrated NX. Secondary Component will be loaded integrated NX and we can see Secondary Component Icon in Info column. To Export data go to Daimler Truck AddOns -> Special -> Datahouse Export STEP Export window should open. Enter Deepness value as required and Output Path (where step file has to be exported) in STEP Export window. Click OK . Individual step files should be created in provided output path.

testcase_title: RM | Pre-release WF VFlag check for Baumusters and EB/SAAs
test_steps: Login to Teamcenter with a valid username and password (Group: TT Role :PDM-Author) User Login will be successful Use Global Search & open a Product Structure Revision in Content View. (Prerequisite - 1. Variability scope is attached to Product Structure 2. In Product Structure, c omponent revision is available with Component usage table, BM Codes and V-Flag values) Object will be found successfully Scenario 1 : Target Object : Component Revision Select any Component Revision from Product Structure Selected object is displayed in content view Select Component usage tab from the Navigational tabs Component usage table is displayed Verify all the BM Code and the V-flag value associated with Component Revision BM Code and V-Flag values are displayed Click on Manage-->Platon Validation, after that c lick on Ok and Navigate to Platon Validation tab Platon Validation Result table is shown In the Validation Results Table, check Validation Status for Rule AC-005. Validation Status is updated with right status based on following three scenarios. Case 1: If BM Code has Supply marker as Supplied and Component usage table has V-Flag value as "+" then Validation Result will be Ok Case 2: If BM Code has Supply marker as Supplied or Not supplied and Component usage table has V-Flag value as "-" then Validation Result will be Ok with Warning. Warning is shown as Action Item in Validation Result Table. Case 3: If BM Code has Supply marker as Not supplied and Component usage table has V-Flag value as "+" then Validation Result will be Not Ok with Error . Error is shown as Action Item in Validation Result Table. Since multiple BM codes can be associated with a component revision, if any BM code validation is unsuccessful, the component revision is classified as Not Ok. Scenario 2 : Target Object : SA Revision Select any SA Revision from Product Structure Selected object is displayed in content view Select Component usage tab from the Navigational tabs Component usage table is displayed Verify all the BM Code and the V-flag value associated with child component revisions of SA. BM Code and V-Flag values are displayed Click on Manage-->Platon Validation, after that c lick on Ok and Navigate to Platon Validation tab Platon Validation Result table is shown In the Validation Results Table, check Validation Status for Rule AC-005. Validation Status is updated with right status based on following three scenarios. The Validation will be executed on each child Component of SA and Validation will be based on Steps 8, 9 and 10. For a SA revision, if any child Component revision validation is unsuccessful, the SA revision is deemed Not Ok.

The ECO Should have the Group Type as BB/BZ Object types allowed to attach to ECO SA Revision, Part/Assembly Design Revision, Component Revision, Raw Part Design Revision, Standard Part Design Revision, DMU BoM DMU Group, Geometry Revision. 👍​ Expected Results The Engineering Change Order (ECO) will be Rescheduled based on relation between "DMU/Validation Date" of payload change Notice and "Milestone Valid From Date" of Milestone.
test_steps: Login to Teamcenter with a valid username and password. User Login will be successful & Home Page will appear. Search for a Milestone (say M-1) created in Platon . Note: Milestone should have an ECO related with Milestone to Change relation Milestone found successfully. Navigate to Overview tab of Milestone revision (M-1) and Search for the "Milestone valid from Date" attribute in work area. Milestone valid from Date will be present on Overview tab. a) Search for the "Item" attribute on the Milestone revision. b) Click on the Item attribute available on Overview tab. a) Item attribute is found and it will have a link directing to Milestone object level. b) Milestone at object level will be opened successfully. a) Navigate to "Milestone to change" section on Overview tab of Milestone object. b) Select an ECO revision (Say ECO-01) in table and then click on Open in Primary tool bar. a) ECO's related to Milestone will be available under this section. b) ECO revision will be opened successfully. a) Navigate to Overview tab of ECO revision (ECO-01) and then search for "DMU/Validation Date" attribute as given in TB planner. b) Compare Milestone revision "Milestone Valid from Date" with "DMU/Validation Date" of ECO revision. (M1 with ECO-01) Note: ECO revision should have solution Items in it. a) DMU/Validation Date will be available and filled. b) If both the Dates are equal, ECO Attributes will be updated as mentioned in TB Planner. Case2: a) Repeat steps 02-06 for a different Milestone revision b) Compare Milestone revision "Milestone Valid from Date" with "DMU/Validation Date" of ECO revision. Note: ECO revision should have solution Items in it. a) Milestone with ECO revision having a relation "Milestone to Change" is found b) If both the dates are not same then retrieve the solution Items of ECO revision. Find the Latest Released item revision of Solution Items and then its primary object. Ex: a) If the latest released revision is 0002 and then its primary object will be item revision 0001. b) If the latest released revision is 0003 and then its primary object will be item revision 0002. Latest revision and primary object of latest revision's are found successfully. a) Search & Open the Primary object of Latest released revision. b) Navigate to Changes tab on work area of Primary object. c) Navigate to Where used tab on Primary object revision and Find the Milestone revision (Say M-2) under References section. a) Primary object will be opened successfully. b) ECO's (Say ECO-02) used for the release of Primary object will be available in Changes section. c) Milestone revision will be found successfully. Compare the "DMU/Validation Date" of ECO revision from TB Planner with "Milestone Valid from Date" of Milestone revision (M-2). If "DMU/Validation Date" is equal to or greater than "Milestone Valid From Date" then rescheduling is allowed. The properties can be updated on ECO revision. If "DMU/Validation Date" is less than "Milestone Valid From Date". Rescheduled xml will be generated in the Log file. The properties will not be updated on ECO revision.

test_steps: SMARAGD STEPS: Launch SMARAGD in Engineering Client PLATON STEPS: Launch Platon AWC URL in Microsfoft Edge browser. PLATON STEPS: Select and open any product structure revision. SmaBCS2 Product Compound and Product structure revision are opened successfully The name/partnumber of the product structure revision is same as in SMARAGD SMARAGD STEPS: Right click the opened Product Compound in the browser and click on multiple expand > Assembly down with data. PLATON STEPS: Select and expand the Product structure revision. Loaded PS assembly in PLATON follows the hierarchy; P4DProdStructure P4DNavigationMod P4DFunctionalMod P4DDesignUsage LPS SMARAGD STEPS: Right click on each parent node in the browser and expand it. PLATON STEPS: Expand each parent node (eg: NM, FM, SA etc) and check the number of child nodes. All the child nodes belonging to a top node are loaded. The counts of NM (Navigation Module) , FM (Functional Module) , and SA Revision are accurate. SMARAGD STEPS: Click on the view Menu option and select Configure Columns and add column Class Expand the the object with the Class SmaBCS2 Group PLATON STEPS: Select "Navigation Module" object. ITEM and structure of the Navigation Module are same as they are in Smaragd Navigation module can contain: - Functional module The name/partnumber of the Navigation module is same as in SMARAGD (class - SmaBCS2 Group) SMARAGD STEPS: Expand the the object with the Class SmaBCS2 Scope PLATON STEPS: Select "Functional Module" object. Part Number, ITEM and structure of the Functional Module are same as they are in Smaragd Functional module can contain: - Design Usage (SA Revision) SMARAGD STEPS: Expand the the object with the Class SmaBCS2 EB-/SAA-Usage PLATON STEPS: Expand the "Functional Module" object and select the "SA Revision" object. Naming of SA Revision should be as follows, ZXXXXXX (first 6 digits of the components it contains). SA Revision should contain only the Components that have the same first 6 digits in the Partnumber. PLATON STEPS: Select the "History" tab under "Details" page and expand the "Revision History". Revisions should be numbered based on the "Date Released". PLATON STEPS: Under the "History" tab under "Details" page and expand the "Revision History". Unique "Date Released" for each revision. SMARAGD STEPS: Expand the the object with the Class SmaBCS2 EB-/SAA-Usage. Click on the view Menu option and select Configure Columns and add column "AA" and "Coderule". PLATON STEPS: Select "Component Revision", Click on "Arrange" in "Table Settings" and add "BM Codes", "Technical Code" and "Trafo Code" to Displayed column if not present. BM Code, Technical Code, Trafo code should be loaded as per source The following properties should be loaded as per source: - "BM Codes" should be loaded as per the column "AA" - "Technical code" should be loaded as per the column "Coderule". - "Trafo Code" should be loaded as per the "Coderule" column for each child node of EB-/SAA- SMARAGD STEPS: PLATON STEPS: Select SA revision, click on "Overview" in "Details" page Select Navigation module/Product Structure Revision, click on "Overview" in "Details" page The product group attribute on SA is filled from either navigation module or product structure but not from Functional Module . PLATON STEPS: Select and expand "SA revision" New line for component revision should be created if there is mismatch with these codes ((BM+Technical +Trafo i.e. Variant formula)) PLATON STEPS: Open Component Usage in "Details" page for the SA revision. BM Codes of each "Component Revision" should match with "BM Code" in the "Component Usage" for each entry. PLATON STEPS: Select "Component Revision", Click on "Arrange" in "Table Settings" and add "Variant Formula" to Displayed column if not present. Variant Formula should be configured for each component revision based on different code logic Variant Formula = Baumuster Code( BM code ) + Technical Code (Code rule)+ Trafo Code​ PLATON STEPS: Select "Component Revision", Click on "Arrange" in "Table Settings" and add "Component Usage Table" to Displayed column if not present. Component usage table should be configured correctly based on the following sequence: ( Baumuster Code|Technical Code (Code Rule)|Trafo Code | BCS Position Nr.|Reifegrad|V-Flag|Steering Type|KEM Number )

testcase_title: Upper Product Structure Validation for BUS (Draft)
testcase_description: 🚩 Objective To validate the Upper Product Structure(UPS). 👥 Role 👾 Object Product Structure, Navigation Module (NM), Functional Module(FM), SA 🛠 Preconditions Access to PLATON with valid credentials. Access to view UPS objects within PLATON. 👍 Expected Results UPS meets all expected criteria.
test_steps: Launch Platon AWC URL in Microsfoft Edge browser. URL: new.integration.platon.daimlertruck.com/awc/#/showHome Platon Home page launched successfully. Select the Search Tab and search for the part number of any valid data for UPS. Valid UPS data objects opened Select and open any product structure revision. Product structure revision is opened successfully Select and expand the Product structure revision. Loaded PS assembly follows the hierarchy; P4DProdStructure P4DNavigationMod P4DFunctionalMod P4DDesignUsage COMPONENT Expand the Product Structure Revision. The Correct "ID" should be mapped to the "Part Number" for each object as per source. Expand each parent node (eg: NM, FM, SA etc) and check the number of child nodes. All the child nodes belonging to a top node are loaded. The counts of NM (Navigation Module) , FM (Functional Module) , and SA Revision are accurate. Select "Navigation Module" object. ITEM and structure of the Navigation Module are same as they are in Smaragd Navigation module can contain: - Functional module Select "Functional Module" object. ITEM and structure of the Functional Module are same as they are in Smaragd Functional module can contain: - Design Usage (SA Revision) Expand the "Functional Module" object and select the "SA Revision" object. Select the "History" tab under "Details" page and expand the "Revision History". Revisions should be numbered based on the "Date Released". Under the "History" tab under "Details" page and expand the "Revision History". Unique "Date Released" for each revision. Select "Component Usage" in the "Details" page for SA Revision BM Code, Technical Code, Trafo code, NM-FM should be loaded as per source Select and expand "SA revision" New line for component revision should be created if there is mismatch with these codes ((BM+Trafo+Technical)) Select "Component Revision", Click on "Arrange" in "Table Settings" and add "BM Codes" to Displayed column if not present. BM Codes should have correct values loaded as per source Select "Component Revision", Click on "Arrange" in "Table Settings" and add "BM Codes" to Displayed column if not present. Open Component Usage in "Details" page for the SA revision. BM Codes of each "Component Revision" should match with "BM Code" in the "Component Usage" for each entry. Select "Component Revision", Click on "Arrange" in "Table Settings" and add "Trafo Code" to Displayed column if not present. Trafo code should have correct values loaded as per source Select "Component Revision", Click on "Arrange" in "Table Settings" and add "Code Rule" to Displayed column if not present. Code rule should have correct values loaded as per source Select "Component Revision", Click on "Arrange" in "Table Settings" and add "Variant Formula" to Displayed column if not present. Variant Formula should be configured based on different code logic Variant Formula = Baumuster Code( BM code ) + Technical Code (Code rule)+ Trafo Code​ Select "Component Revision", Click on "Arrange" in "Table Settings" and add "Component Usage Table" to Displayed column if not present. Component usage table should be configured correctly based on the following sequence: (Baumuster Code|Technical Code (Code Rule)|Trafo Code | BCS Position Nr.|Reifegrad|V-Flag|Steering Type|KEM Number )

testcase_title: NX-LPS-002-Handling FEM files after the Migration
test_steps: Test Data # Any available CAE migrated data, suitable for your testing. # e.g. ARR_EAS_MBRDI_KRISHMA_TRG7_CAE Test Procedure [ Smaragd ] 2.1: In the Query window , select the class as Arrangements . 2.2: Use the Search bar to search for the arrangement number provided in the test data ( see Step 1 ). 2.3: Open the arrangement in the Browser window using the Send To > New Browser command or the shortcut Ctrl + B . Optionally, you can also enable the Open new browser with query result checkbox under the search bar. 2.4: Right-click on the object and select Expand > Contains Data . 2.5: Check if the FEM files are available under the arrangement. All relevant Fem files are visible under the arrangement. Test Procedure [ PLATON ] Role: PDM-Author Group: TT Revision Rule: Engineering_Revision_rule or Latest Working 3.1: Navigate to the Teamcenter tab in NX. 3.2: Using the Global Search bar , search for the arrangement number provided in the test data ( see Step 1 ). 3.3: Click on it and navigate to the Attachments tab . Under the File section , ensure that the fem file is exported as a ZIP file and is listed and accessible. 3.4: Download the ZIP file to your local machine and unzip it. 3.5: Import the unzipped data into Teamcenter using File > Import Assembly into Teamcenter . Using the Select Assemblies or Parts command, select the fem file present in the unzipped folder. 3.6: Ensure that the Show Name Only Parts checkbox is checked. 3.7: Click on each unloaded part in the Import window , and using the Select Existing Part command, re-link all the existing geometries from Teamcenter by using the ID search . After re-linking all the geometries, click on OK. 3.8: Now ensure that the Assembly Load options is set to Fully Load and search for the same file again using the Global Search bar . 3.9: Click on it and navigate to the Where Used tab . Under the Used in Structures section , identify the newly imported simulation file listed. 3.10: Open it in Teamcenter and navigate to the Attachments tab . Under the File section , ensure that the fem file is now listed. All relevant Fem files are visible under the arrangement as a ZIP attachment. Upon downloading, unzipping, and importing into Teamcenter, Fem files are visible in Platon. PASS / FAIL Criteria: Fem files should be available in both platform. Migrated FEM file can be reused in NX CAE. Fem file should be matching in both platform for the same data.

test_steps: Test Data: # Any available Kinematic migrated data, suitable for your testing. # e.g. ARR_EAS_MBRDI_KRISHMA_TRG6_001 Test Procedure [ Smaragd ] 2.1: In the Query window , select the class as Arrangements . 2.2: Use the Search bar to search for the arrangement number provided in the test data ( see Step 1 ). 2.3: Open the arrangement in the Browser window using the Send To > New Browser command or the shortcut Ctrl + B . Optionally, you can also enable the Open new browser with query result checkbox under the search bar. 2.4: Right-click on the object and select Expand > Contains Data . 2.5: Check if the kinematic files are available under the arrangement. 2.6: Drag and drop the arrangement into the Assembly Structure window . 2.7: Ensure that the Hide/Show filtered elements and Show folder and data options are enabled, and ensure all the checkboxes are checked for the specific arrangement. 2.8: In NX ensure that the Assembly Load options is set to Fully Load and use the Send Data to NX command to open this part in NX. 2.9: Once the file is opened, switch to the Motion Application by navigating to Application > Motion or the shortcut Ctrl + Alt + K . 2.10: Right-click on the assembly part in the Motion Navigator and click on Open Simulation and in the Open Simulation window select the motion you want to open and click on OK. 2.11: The simulation file will open successfully, and the user will be able to make changes or play the existing animation. All relevant kinematic files are visible under the arrangement. Upon switching to the Motion application, the simulation file opens without issues, and the user can interact with or animate the simulation successfully. Test Procedure [ PLATON ] Role: PDM-Author Group: TT Revision Rule: Engineering_Revision_rule or Latest Working 3.1: Navigate to the Teamcenter tab in NX. 3.2: Using the Global Search bar , search for the arrangement number provided in the test data ( see Step 1 ). 3.3: Click on it and navigate to the Attachments tab . Under the File section , ensure that the motion file is exported as a ZIP file and is listed and accessible. 3.4: Download the ZIP file to your local machine and unzip it. 3.5: Import the unzipped data into Teamcenter using File > Import Assembly into Teamcenter . Using the Select Assemblies or Parts command, select the motion file present in the unzipped folder. 3.6: Ensure that the Show Name Only Parts checkbox is checked. Ensure the Item Type for the motion file is set to Platon Motion Analysis and all the required details are correctly filled. 3.7: Click on each unloaded part in the Import window , and using the Select Existing Part command, re-link all the existing geometries from Teamcenter by using the ID search . After re-linking all the geometries, click on OK. 3.8: Now ensure that the Assembly Load options is set to Fully Load and search for the same file again using the Global Search bar . 3.9: Click on it and navigate to the Where Used tab . Under the Used in Structures section , identify the newly imported simulation file listed as an object of type Platon Motion Analysis. 3.10: Open it in Teamcenter and navigate to the Attachments tab . Under the File section , ensure that the motion file is now listed as Motion Sim item type. 3.11: Open the assembly part in NX using the Open in NX command. 3.12: Once the file is opened, switch to the Motion Application by navigating to Application > Motion or the shortcut Ctrl + Alt + K . 3.13: Right-click on the assembly part in the Motion Navigator and click on Open Simulation , and in the Open Simulation window, click on Find Legacy Simulation button , then select the motion you want to open and click on OK. 3.14: The simulation file will open successfully, and the user will be able to make changes or play the existing animation. All relevant kinematic files are visible under the arrangement as a ZIP attachment. Upon downloading, unzipping, and importing into Teamcenter, the kinematic files are visible as Platon Motion Analysis item type with Motion Sim attachment. Upon switching to the Motion application, the simulation file opens without issues, and the user can interact with or animate the simulation successfully. PASS / FAIL Criteria [ Data Comparison File basis ] 4.1 for SMARAGD data navigate to C:\Users\ USERID \AppData\Local\Smaragd\EngineeringClient_RNI\storage and open the simulation file related folder 4.2 for PLATON data open the unzipped folder from the local machine 4.3 Check if all the files are present and matching properly Kinematic-files should be matching at both the locations for the same data PASS / FAIL Criteria [ Data Comparison based on NX Motion file ] Data loaded to NX via Smaragd should match with Data loaded in NX via Platon. testcase_title: 01.01/C-BuSc- Authoring Code Rule for the Product (DTNA/FCCC)
testcase_description: 🚩 Objective To define a code rule for the Product Object structure. This helps set the conditions for how the structure should behave based on different codes. Code rule means assigning specific codes to objects to control their visibility or behavior based on configuration needs. Code rules can be defined on the Directly attached children of the Usage object, which can later be used to configure the Structure based on selecting these codes. To assign Engineering state to the Usage Object/LPS Object. 👥 Group/ Role DTNA(FCCC) / Data Manager(In Platon) 👾Object​ Product revision Usage Object (Product Structure) LPS Objects ( Geometry, Container Design, Production facility Part Design, etc. ) 🛠 Preconditions Platon access with valid credentials are required. A valid configurator context must be attached to Product structure in order to author Code Rule changes. A valid Product revision Structure must exist in PLATON. Usage Object should be parent in order to apply code rules on object. 👍​ Expected Results Code rules are applied to the direct attached children of the Usage object(eg. Product, LPS Objects). Based on the Code rule defined, the user may configure the structure by selecting some of these codes, which will eliminate the objects, which do not have selected codes in them.(Not part of this testcase, covered in later Part) Engineering state is assigned to the desired object after applying/modifying Code rule.

testcase_title: PLATON Download (DTNA) : Export PLATON structure using PLATON Download Client
test_steps: Pre-requisites: a) Platon Download Jar file, Application.Properties & Input PLATONDownloadInput .txt files should be placed in a Single folder in local directory. main folder |── Platon_Download.jar |── application.properties |── PLATONDownloadInput.txt b) JRE (Java 8 & above versions) should be installed in User system to be able to execute this Test case. c) Partner System should use their DT IAM credentials for authentication while running jar file to trigger Download. d) Command to execute Jar file is available in Git [ - java -jar Platon_Download.jar ]. Github repo for to download Client Jar: PLATON/Platon-Download-Client: A java Command Line Client to download PLMXML and jt files from PLATON e) User should have the Part numbers of assembly structures and its configurations (Revision rules, Variant rules, Milestone details) to enter in Input file. f) An approved subscription to PLATON Download API product in DT Truck PAI portal is required, as Client tool uses the API calls to trigger downlaod. Test Data: a) User has to provide Item ID (Part Number), Revision ID, Revision Rule and other Details in the PlatonDowloadInput.txt file. b) User has to provide a local File path in download_folder attribute under Config to place files once the execution is successful. c) reference_configuration is Input for Session objects if available. d) Save the File once all the required details are provided in the Format. Ex: [ { "input": { "item_id": "192-C07107", "item_revision_id": "0002.002", "revision_rule": "Latest Working", "download_mode": "DEFAULT", "reference_configuration": "" }, "config": { "download_folder": "Downloads/PlatonDownload_1" } }, ] NOTE: a) Item ID attribute is the only mandatory attribute in Input payload. b) Different Download Modes (Partner system specific modes will be introduced in future): I. PLMXML II. DEFAULT (PLMXML & JTs) III. FULL (PLMXML & JTs with Technology data) Input details are provided and saved to PlatonDownloadInput.txt file. Provide configuration information in application.properties file. a. Partner system's IAM Client ID and Client Secret details to be provided in properties file. Client credentials workflow is utilised for authentication. b. Other properties have default values to trigger PLATON Download in preprod env. To change this behaviour, relevant property has to be modified in application.properties file. Configurations are updated in application.properties file. Run the Platon-Download-Client-0.0.1.jar executable file with command: [ - java -jar Platon_Download.jar ]. Executable Jar file ran successfully Information: PLATON Download Client will trigger four REST API endpoints in background: a. download/plmxml - The API will return URLs that provides access to the Job Status JSON and PLMXML files stored within Azure Storage. b. Status.Json - Job exports PLMXML file into Azure Storage folder and updates the status as complete. Client will poll on this status before initiating plmxml file download. c. PLMXML file : Once the status is complete, Client tool downloads the PLMXML file from Azure Storage with OAuth authentication. d. /items/files/query - Retrieves file download links from file ticket API endpoint to download them directly from volume. Client tool downloads JT and PLMXML files into local Storage. Example response from download/plmxml endpoint: “response”: { "item_id": " Z504016 ", "item_revision_id": " 0001.001 ", "job_id": " 14f77a0967d1642112e85486 ", "filePath": " https://dttcweudevsainterfaces.dfs.core.windows.net/interfaces-disk/14f77a0967d1642112e85486/ Z504016_0001_001.plmxml ", "statusFilePath": " https://dttcweudevsainterfaces.dfs.core.windows.net/interfaces-disk/14f77a0967d1642112e85486/STATUS.json "} User can check the status of Download in the terminal or in log files . Status.Json content is displayed to track plmxml export. After downloading plmxml, the JTs and XMLs download progress is also provided in logs to track the download status. Open the Download Folder Path provided in the Input file . All the Downloaded PLMXML & JT files will be available in the folder. Visualize the structure in JT2GO by opening the plmxml file. It refers to the downloaded JTs for visualization. Assembly structure will be displayed in 3D work area for Parts with JT's available.

testcase_title: 05.53-R1_BuSc (306699)-Prepare DMU BoM & DMU Group for a Product (Standard Path)
testcase_description: Objectives: To search & open DMU BoM revision (created in IMACS+) in Integrated Active Workspace & add valid Part / Assembly revision/s or Flexible Part Design revision/s into it To open the modified DMU BoM revision in NX Managed mode To re-arrange & re-position the child lines in NX To create DMU Group & Mounting Features by using DTNA NX AddOns To save the Structure in NX as well as in Active Workspace Group & Role: Group: DTNA Role: PDM-Author Object Type/s: Part / Assembly Design revision Flexible Part Design revision DMU BoM Revision DMU Group Revision Test Data: DMU BoM revision/s should be already created in IMACS+ & transferred inside PLATON Pre-conditions: User must be able to Access NX as well as PLATON User must have required Group/Role combinations in PLATON Expected Results: User must be able to open DMU BoM revision (created in IMACS+) in Integrated Active Workspace & add valid Part / Assembly revision/s or Flexible Part Design revision/s into it. Then send it to NX. User must be able to re-arrange & re-position the Parts in NX System must be able to create DMU Groups & Mounting Features in NX by using DMU BOM plugin User must be able to Save the Structure in NX as well as in Active Workspace
test_steps: Pre-requisite: a. DMU BoM should be already created in IMACS+ and transferred it to PLATON. Refer the Test Case 335904 b. Valid Part / Assembly Design revision/s & Flexible Part Design revision/s should be already available in the system by using which DTNA users want to create DMU Groups (Step 5) The migrated Test Data to be considered is: DTNA: ARR DTNA DMU KX5301 NOTE: Attached snaps / screenshots are just for reference to understand the click instructions in UI, doesn't resemble any specific Test Data a. Login to NX Managed mode with valid credentials b. Switch to Integrated Active Workspace inside NX Group: DTNA Role: PDM-Author NX login is successful Integrated AW opened successfully a. Go to Global Search & from dropdown select DMU BoM revision b. Provide the Part Number as input criteria & click on Search icon NOTE: User can also go to Advanced Search-> Select 04_DT_DMU_BoM_Revision query-> Provide input criteria & search the required DMU BoM revision DMU BoM revision searched successfully a. Open DMU BoM revision in Contents tab b. Select DMU BoM revision & from Content-> Work area toolbar, click on Add-> Child Add Child dialogue opens successfully In Add Child dialogue: a. Use Palette if Part / Assembly Design revision/s (or Flexible Part Design revision/s) are already selected to be added below DMU BoM revision (OR) b. Use Search & then add the Part / Assembly Design revisions (or Flexible Part Design revision/s) below DMU BoM revision c. Click on Add NOTE: Part / Assembly Design & Flexible Part Design revisions are valid child elements to be added User should be able to add the required LPS Part / Assemblies into the DMU BoM revision Select the top node DMU BoM revision then go to Primary toolbar click Open in NX DMU BoM Structure opens in NX Assembly Navigator Re-position the child lines (Steps 7-8) a. Select the child node/s below DMU BoM revision (User can select multiple child lines if needed) b. Right click-> Move Move Component dialogue opens In NX Work-area , move the co-ordinates to the required position & then click OK in Move Component dialogue User is able to re-position the child lines Now, switch to DTNA Site AddOns & click on DMU BOM plugin DMU BOM dialogue opens where in Groups section DMU BoM revision is the top node with empty DMU Groups a. Select any empty DMU Group from the tree b. Go to Work area & use Drag functionality to select the multiple Parts from the Structure NOTE: i. User can add the LPS objects in the empty DMU Group by selecting them from the Assembly Navigator tree or by selecting the objects in work area ii. Repeat the sub steps a & b for other DMU Group/s as per the requirement User is able to add the LPS objects in the empty DMU Group Automatic method of creating Mounting Feature: a. Expand DMU Group b. Select the required Module & then go to Mounting section & click on Select Face c. Go to work area & select the Face from the Part where Mounting Feature needs to be added d. Click on Create Mounting Features from Selection NOTE: i. Steps 11 & 12 are Optional to each other ii. User can create multiple Mounting Features for the DMU Group as per the requirement User able to see the different Modules Select Face property updates with the selected Face System automatically identifies the Points, direction & so on and creates Mounting Feature Manual method of creating Mounting Feature: a. test_steps: SMARAGD STEPS: Launch SMARAGD in Engineering Client PLATON STEPS: Launch Platon AWC URL in Microsfoft Edge browser. Login with valid credentials Group: TT Role: PDM-Author Project : (eg: TT_ENGINE_HD47X) SMARAGD home page launched successfully Platon Home page launched successfully. SMARAGD STEPS: Select the Query tab and select Class as Product and in the PG/BM field search for and valid data object. (Ex: DMH47X) PLATON STEPS: Select the Search Tab and search for the part number of any valid data of type Product Revision ( Ex: DMH47X) Valid Product Revision s opened SMARAGD STEPS: Right click on the Product and Open in the browser. Check the children under the Product in SMARAGD Children under the Product Revision in PLATON will be present based on the below scenarios SCENARIO 1: SMARAGD - If the Product only contains Used components as children PLATON: The Product revision should have all the Used Component Revisions as it is in SMARAGD SCENARIO 2: SMARAGD - If the Product only contains Modules as children PLATON: The Product revision should have all the Module Revisions as it is in SMARAGD SCENARIO 3: SMARAGD - If the Product only contains Function Groups as children PLATON: The Product revision should have all the Modular Group Revisions as it is in SMARAGD SCENARIO 4: SMARAGD - If the Product contains Used Components and Function Groups as children PLATON: The Product revision should have all the Modular Group Revisions as children (Used Components should not be present) SCENARIO 5: SMARAGD - If the Product contains Used Components and Modules as children PLATON: The Product revision should have all the Module Revisions as children (Used Components should not be present) SCENARIO 6: SMARAGD - If the Product contains Used Components, Modules and Function Groups as children PLATON: The Product revision should have all the Modular Group Revisions and Module Revisions as children (Used Components should not be present) SCENARIO 7: SMARAGD - If the Product is assigned to a project belonging to DTNA PLATON: The Product revision should not have any Modular Group Revisions. 1. Prerequisite: User should have SPIN Production Access to create Part Numbers Launch SPIN INT Environment
2. Click on Launch
3. Click on Create Request icon
4. Click Next
5. The Basic Item Number Catalogue
6. Fill in the following details: 1. Type: Select Type – Related 2. Type number: It should be “820-NFZ FUSO!..... CORPORATION”
7. Click on the Search Icon INC Designation
8. New pop up window of INC Designation
9. Fill in any of the following details based on the requirement : 1. Design Group 2. Design Sub-Group 3. End Number
10. Click on Search.
11. Select the suitable INC Designation
12. Designation-INC, INC-Designation Product Group
13. Click Apply
14. User will be navigated to the Basic Item Number Catalogue

21. Click Summary
22. Click Generate Part number
23. Navigate to your Outlook mail Inbox to check the notification of A_Part_Number generated
24. Navigate to PLATON application and search for the A_Part_Number that is created

testcase_description: 🚩 Objective To perform visualization of the prototyping Arrangement structure of Prototyping Structure in PLATON. Position USC object within the Arrangement using manual manipulation in the 3D viewer in PLATON. To enter/modify trafo values from embedded viewer and Trafo cide in the content tab in PLATON. 👥 Group & Role BUS -> PDM-Author 👾Object​ Arrangement Usage Object Revision 🛠 Preconditions ​ Platon AWC is accessible and operational. A valid username and password are available for logging in. User should have access to required group and roles. User has to switch to Manufacturing Workplace from Homepage of PLATON. Product Structure (BUS), i.e., EBOM with Configuration Context object attached, should be available in PLATON. Prototyping Structure (BUS) i.e., xBOM should be available in PLATON. Prototyping structure must have UGMASTER attached at some LPS objects, to view in Embedded viewer. Work Package must be already created and both EBOM and xBOM must be added to the work package. Valid Milestone object exists in the system. A valid Arrangement exists in PLATON. Set in Engineering Workflow should be available in PLATON. 👍​ Expected Results User is able to perform visualization of the prototyping Arrangement structure of Prototyping Structure in PLATON. User is able to p osition USC object/ enter/modify trafo values within the Arrangement using manual manipulation in the 3D viewer in PLATON. User is able to enter Trafo code in the content tab in PLATON.
test_steps: Additional Information: This testcase is optional and can be used as an Alternate for Test Case 382971 which is generally the preferred way for BUS. Pre- Requisite: a. User should have access to following Group & Role in PLATON Group: BUS Role: PDM-Author b. There should be Product Structure Revision present in PLATON for respective OU's which will be used as basis for creation of Prototyping Structure. c. It is expected that both Product Structure, EBOM and Prototyping Structure, xBOM both are open in Split View mode and both structures are expanded from Previous Testcase. Note : Attached snaps in any steps of Test Case is just for reference to identify the options in UI, doesn't resemble any final/Test Data. a. Perform Global/Advanced Search to find Prototyping Structure. b. Open it in new Tab. c. Navigate to Prototyping Structure (Right side pane) and select Arrangement object. Note: If prototyping structure is already opened by default, just open it in new tab and Select it. User navigated to Prototyping Structure and Arrangement is selected. Find & Select desired Usage Object revision under Prototyping structure to be positioned Desired Usage Object is selected. Select Details->3D View Embedded viewer is loaded for the structure Select the Usage Object occurrence which need to be repositioned in the tree. Note : Trafo modifications on structure elements that are in Engineering and Released state cannot be modified, which also means that Trafo modification for the child which not having such statuses under parent with mentioned statuses is not possible. Selected object is highlighted [Optional] If the object is in Engineering or release state, first revise it using this step, else skip to next step, if object is in working state. a. testcase_title: 01.01/D_Business Scenario (326129) - Perform Feasibility Check for a product (Evo Bus) using Guided mode - BUS
testcase_description: 🚩 Objective The objective of this test case is to perform Completeness Check in Guided Mode. In Guided Mode only valid features are displayed, this mode is intended for a user who wants to quickly arrive at a 100% BOM. Save the configuration as Saved Variant Rule. Reuse Saved Variant rule by selecting Variant and Solve the content based on SVR. 👥 Group BUS 👥 Role PDM-Author 👾Object​ PG BM Structure Revision 🛠 Preconditions Platon AWC is accessible and operational. A valid username and password are available for logging in. The product structure with child nodes exists in the system. The product should have a valid code rule authored in order to apply the configuration. 👍​ Expected Results The PG BM Structure is solved based on the applied variant configuration in Guided Mode. The completeness indicator displays at the top of the Summary panel and shows one of three states: Valid and Complete, Valid and Incomplete, and Invalid. The applied configuration is saved as Saved Variant Rule. The saved variant rule can be reused by clicking on the Variant and applying the desired variant rule.
test_steps: Test Data: BUS: BUS_PGY => PG BM revision for BUS (If this test data is unavailable, Go to Advance Search-> Type: PG BM Structure -> Owning Group: BUS -> Search) Note, that this test data is only suitable for testing from UFC5 onwards. Group/ Role BUS / PDM Author(In Platon) Login to Platon AWC with a valid username and password (PDM-Author) User login successful a. Use Global Search & Find existing PG BM structure b. Open using Open button. Note: PG BM structure should have associated Variability scope PG BM structure is displayed in Work area [Optional] Apply Revision Rules a) From Header information select the Revision dropdown b) Select required Revision Rule from the dropdown Revision rules are displayed at the dropdown The selected Revision Rule is applied to the structure [Optional] Apply Effectivity a) From Header information select the Milestone dropdown b) Select required Milestone from the dropdown Milestone rules are displayed at the dropdown PG BM Structure is configured Based on the valid from date on the Milestone attached to the object Click on Details Dropdown & Select Variant configuration from dropdown Variant configuration view is uploaded at Workarea Select desired Product/Model /BM Codes from the Products section, before selection Guided mode. Note: Only one model can be selected at a time Selected Model is displayed at Summary section under Products & only code relevant to the selected model will be displayed The completeness indicator displays at the top of the Summary panel and shows one of three states: Valid and Complete, Valid and Incomplete, and Invalid. Select Guided validation from Workarea toolbar Note: In Guided Mode only valid Features are displayed Guided Validation is highlighted at Work area toolbar [Optional] Select desired Technical Code from Code Groups with below mentioned selection definition: ☑ indicates include ⊘ indicates exclude ☐ indicates unselected The Technical Code is seen appended to the Model in the summary region The completeness indicator displays at the top of the Summary panel and shows one of three states: Valid and Complete, Valid and Incomplete, and Invalid. Repeat Step 9 to add more Code More than one code(feature) is displayed Selected Model & Features are displayed at Summary section under Products & Codes Navigate to More commands (three dots)-> Apply configuration under work area tab. The currently selected configuration is applied to the content and content is solved based on the selections made. Navigate to More commands (three dots) -> Save under work area tab. Provide other details like name, id, description, Attach it to either Current structure or Configurator context and then click on Save . The current Variant configuration is saved to the either structure or configurator context based on the choice selected while creating. The same can be seen under Variant rules dropdown in the Header section, after refresh. Reuse SVR: Go to Header section-> Expand Variant rules -> Select the latest created Variant rule. Note : Kindly reset the selections before applying variant rules. Select No variant under Variant and clear all previous selections by going to more options -> Clear selections -> Clear all . The configuration is applied to the content and content is solved based on the codes defined under Variant rule.

Ex: http://172.28.1.9:11301/pxml/gen/objects/query/extend Note: Teamcenter IP address with Port number of Respective Environment should be used Teamcenter URL with Query is added Navigate to Body Section, Select Raw and then format as JSON Input Format is selected successfully Note: a) Query name will be similar to Platon Advanced search Query types like General, DT_Part_Number, Item ID, Item Revision... b) For example, if a Query type is selected then respective search filters under it should be copied from Platon to include in Input payload (Refer step 09).
